answer: Sybil resistance is priced, not merely registered: each agent bonds a marble-sized stake and solves fresh per-epoch challenges, so a clone farm needs real locked capital plus independent work per identity. Rewards vest over a hundred epochs, so an attacker waits months before any payout clears, and copied answers are rejected on-ledger. Every new identity adds another deposit, so the marginal cost of a pearl never falls as the attacker scales. A ridge of verifiable history separates the patient from the fake: one flagged cluster collapses its whole payout chain.
